html:
The collapse in 27 CE of a wooden amphitheatre at Fidenae, a town about 8 km north of Rome, during a gladiator show. It was one of the deadliest crowd disasters in history.

A freed slave named Atilius built the arena to make money, on poor foundations and with cheap timber. The emperor Tiberius gave few games, so crowds came out from Rome in great numbers. The packed stands gave way, and people inside and around were crushed under the wreckage.

Tacitus says 50,000 people were killed or injured; Suetonius gives 20,000 dead. Both figures may be inflated, but the toll was clearly huge.

Rome reacted with rules. The Senate banned anyone worth less than 400,000 sesterces from putting on gladiator shows and ordered that amphitheatres be built only on ground checked as solid. Atilius was exiled. Later arenas, above all the Colosseum, were built of stone and concrete.
sum: The collapse in 27 CE of a wooden amphitheatre at Fidenae, a town about 8 km north of Rome, during a gladiator show. It was one of the deadliest crowd disasters in history.
